questions.question: A rectangular prism is turned upside down. How many faces does it have now?
questions.explain: A rectangular prism always has 6 faces. Turning it upside down does not make any faces disappear.

questions.question: A cube is rolled onto its side. What is it called now?
questions.explain: A cube is still a cube no matter which side it sits on. Rolling it does not change what it is.

questions.question: A cone is turned so the point faces up. What is it still?
questions.explain: A cone is still a cone no matter which way it points. Turning it does not change its shape.

questions.question: A cylinder is laid flat on the floor. Is it still a cylinder?
options: No, it is a flat disc
No, it is a ring now
No, it is a cone now
questions.explain: A cylinder is still a cylinder when it lies on its side. It does not become a flat disc or a ring.

questions.question: Mia picks up a box of crayons and turns it upside down. The box is a rectangular prism. How many edges does it have now?
questions.explain: A rectangular prism always has 12 edges. Turning it upside down does not make any edges go away.

questions.question: Sam draws a triangle on paper. He flips the paper so the point is at the bottom. How many sides does the triangle have?
questions.explain: Flipping the paper does not add or remove sides. The triangle still has 3 sides.

questions.question: Leo turns a prism so it lies on one flat face. What is it still?
questions.explain: A prism stays a prism no matter which face it sits on. Lying it down does not turn it into a flat shape.

questions.question: A child stacks a cube, a sphere, and a cone. She flips the cube over. How many objects changed their shape?
questions.explain: Flipping a cube does not change what it is. None of the three objects changed shape.

questions.question: A rectangular prism has 6 faces and 12 edges. A child turns it upside down, then turns it sideways. How many faces and edges does it have now?
questions.explain: Turning a rectangular prism in any direction does not change its parts. It always has 6 faces and 12 edges.

questions.question: Ana says, 'If I turn a triangle so the point faces down, it is a different shape.' What is wrong with her idea?
options: A point-down shape is a cone
questions.explain: A triangle has 3 sides no matter how you turn it. The point facing down does not change the number of sides.

questions.question: A child turns a cube so it sits on a corner. She sees 3 flat faces and says the cube now has only 3 faces. How many faces does the cube really have?
questions.explain: A cube has 6 faces no matter how it sits. Seeing only 3 does not mean the other 3 are gone.

questions.question: Ali puts 5 rectangular prism blocks in the rectangular prism bin. Then he tips 3 of them onto their sides. How many blocks in the bin are still rectangular prisms?
questions.explain: Tipping a block over does not change what it is, so all 5 blocks are still rectangular prisms. The trap is taking away the 3 tipped blocks.

questions.question: Mia glues 4 paper triangles on a card with their points up. Then she glues 3 more triangles with their points down. How many triangles are on the card?
questions.explain: A triangle with its point down is still a triangle, so count them all: 4 and 3 more makes 7. Do not leave out the turned ones.

questions.question: Sara turns her rectangular prism block upside down. Now she counts 8 corners on it. How many corners did it have before she turned it?
questions.explain: Turning a block never adds or loses corners, so it had 8 corners before too. The trap is thinking a turn changes the parts.

questions.question: Noah stands his rectangular prism block up on its small end. He says, 'Now my block is a cube.' What is wrong with his idea?
options: A block on its end really is a cube.
Standing it up removes two faces.
Turning does not change the block.
A cube turned on its end is a rectangular prism.
questions.explain: A turn or a flip never changes what an object is, so the block is still a rectangular prism. Its faces and edges stay the same as well.
